newsitem.title: INDIA: India stocks fall, Bombay index dives to 3-yr low.
newsitem.headline: India stocks fall, Bombay index dives to 3-yr low.

text.p: Share prices fell in nervous trade across Indian bourses on Tuesday, with Bombay shares leading the free fall, dealers said.
The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) plunged 53.43 points, or 1.87 percent, to close at 2,798.0.
The fall wiped off the market's previous three-year low of 2,811.17 reached on November 19, 1993.
"There is a total absence of buyers in the market. It looks very bad ..." said Kamal Kabra, former president of the BSE.
"Shares are down on low volumes. People are slowly leaving the market."
Traders said selling by local funds coupled with hammering of blue-chip stocks by foreign institutions pulled prices lower.
They said an onslaught of bad news in recent weeks made investors jittery, with some selling pressure seen in smaller stocks across-the-board.
"Small investors are also selling. We are seeing a falling market with no buying support at any level," said chief dealer Ketan Jhaveri at local brokerage Kotak Securities.
Participants said poor six-month results announced by top firms took their toll on market sentiment, with major players taking a bearish look at the market.
"All round selling, mainly by foreign financial institutions pushed share prices down," said Harjit Thakur of Delhi brokers J.S. Chadha and Associates.
ACC fell 35.70 rupees to 930.75, Gujarat Ambuja Cement 11.70 to 191.0, Siemens 38.50 to 347.50, Bajaj Auto 37.0 to 756.0, M&M 9.0 to 266.50, SBI 7.25 to 209.25 and Dr Reddy's 16.50 to 152.50.
The 50-stock National Stock Exchange (NSE) index was off 10.82 points, or 1.3 percent, at 820.25.
